newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan has no immediate comment on Bhutto sacking.
newsitem.headline: Japan has no immediate comment on Bhutto sacking.

text.p: Japan, Pakistan's main aid donor, declined on Tuesday to make any immediate comment on the sacking of Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto, saying it was waiting for the situation to become clearer.
Japan has been Pakistan's biggest aid donor for several years, giving just more than half of the total foreign aid received by Pakistan.

"We are waiting until the situation becomes clearer before issuing a statement," a foreign ministry spokesman told Reuters when asked how Bhutto's sacking would affect Japan's trade and aid relations with Pakistan.
In 1996, Japan extended $542 million in loans to Pakistan, mainly in yen grants for development projects, plus about $70 million in direct aid, Japanese officials said.
The Lahore overhead railroad is the largest aid project, which the Japanese government has financed to the tune of $273 million.

Other major development loans include $135 million for the construction of the Gajibarota hydropower station, $36 million for education projects in Baluchistan and $98 million for sewage system development across the country, according to the officials.
Pakistani President Farooq Leghari sacked Bhutto on Tuesday, accusing her government of widespread corruption and nepotism, and army units took over key installations in Islamabad.
